analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | +1 hike | EPS | distributors desk view 11 Nov 2026
key_insights: Desk view on US distributors: the group has benefited from accelerating inflation (rates, US dollar, CPI, PPI). The desk expects the group as a whole to be a source of funds into year end and 2027.
The desk is surprised that AI disruption, disintermediation and competition from technology has dropped out of the conversation for distributors.
Customer penetration at the point of sale and physical presence (FAST) is seen as a competitive advantage. Ecommerce and book-and-ship businesses (GWW) are seen as more vulnerable.

MSM is the more interesting long among distributors given share opportunities under new management, despite year-to-date gains. WCC has upside optionality to the multiple, the business and management moves.

The desk is cautious on municipal end markets and businesses that almost require inflation (CNM). Competitive pressures remain a multi-year overhang to the multiple at WSO. FERG remains the residential-levered distributor the desk likes despite yesterday's move.

GS added a third 25bp Fed hike in March 2027 to its forecast and still expects a second 25bp hike in December. The October CPI report surprised to the upside across several categories, the third month of worse inflation news.

GS says a third hike could come in January, but March is more likely because it expects softer November and December inflation reports and larger start-of-year price increases boosting January inflation.

GS expects most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot. It says oil futures have fallen substantially since the elections, so the bulk of energy passthrough to consumer prices is behind us.
GS left its terminal fed funds forecast unchanged at 3.25-3.5% and now expects cuts to begin in December 2027 (previously September 2027), followed by cuts in March, June and September 2028.

Pre-market, US markets were up 70bps led by technology after CoreWeave's outlook. Taiwan was up 362bps and KOSPI up 260bps overnight, HSI closed down 98bps, DAX up 80bps. Germany CPI was in line at 2.8%.

WTI is above $87 and Brent $93, up 150bps, as Iran said it will not remove enriched nuclear material from the country and warned a US attack could trigger additional strikes. The 10-year is just below 5%, DXY is above 102 and Bitcoin is flat at $73.9k.

Siemens Energy (ENR GR) rose 8%. Its 2030 targets imply about 7% upgrades to VA, with guided margins of 20-22% against a whisper of 21% or better. The read to electricals depends on whether the 'it's not just datacenters' narrative carries.
Post-market earnings: ATRO, FLY, MRCY and REZI beat on EPS. CNM preannounced Q3 EBITDA below consensus. GGG announced a $600mm accelerated share repurchase.

market_movers.rationale: The desk calls it the more interesting long among distributors, with share opportunities under new management despite year-to-date gains.
The desk says it remains the residential-levered distributor it likes, despite yesterday's move.
Upside optionality to the multiple, the business and any management moves.
Customer penetration at the point of sale and physical presence remain a competitive advantage.
Ecommerce and book-and-ship business models are seen as more vulnerable to technology competition.

A $600mm ASR representing about 5% of shares outstanding, which the desk prefers to a dividend increase or open-ended repurchases.

sector_views.rationale: The desk believes the group as a whole will be a source of funds going forward. Views are mixed across industrial and consumer end markets, and the group has been a beneficiary of accelerating inflation.

earnings_insights: ATRO Q3 reported EPS $0.81 vs consensus $0.72, revenue $272mm vs consensus $268mm, EBITDA $59mm vs consensus $54mm. Bookings $271mm, book-to-bill 1x. Reaffirms revenue guidance, capex lower, IEEPA refunds at the low end of prior range. Call at 4:45pm with a 12% implied move.
CNM preannounced Q3 EBITDA of $267-275mm vs consensus $281mm on sales of $2.12-2.13bn. Full-year guidance EBITDA $950-960mm on sales of $7.8-7.9bn, lower end of EBITDA on similar sales.

FLY Q3 reported EPS loss of 45c vs consensus loss of 50c, revenue $111mm vs consensus $102mm, EBITDA loss $70mm vs consensus loss $78mm. Backlog $1.7bn, up $200mm from the prior quarter. Full-year revenue guidance $440-450mm, top end of prior $420-450mm. Call at 5pm with a 14% implied move.
GGG announced a $600mm accelerated share repurchase, about 5% of shares outstanding.

MRCY fiscal Q1 reported EPS $0.52 vs consensus $0.29, revenue above $253mm vs consensus $243mm, EBITDA $56mm vs consensus $39mm. Q2 revenue up 10% and EBITDA margin up 500bps, rising quarterly the rest of the year. Full-year EBITDA guidance $210mm vs $200mm prior. Revenue growth now double digits vs approaching double digits prior. Bookings $370mm, book-to-bill 1.46x. Call at 5pm with a 15% implied move. CFO Dave Farnworth formally named COO as well.

REZI Q3 reported EPS $0.52 vs consensus $0.34, revenue $727mm at the top end of guidance, EBITDA $154mm vs prior guidance of $145-155mm. Q4 guidance EPS $0.42-0.48 vs consensus $0.34, revenue $710-730mm vs consensus $734mm, EBITDA $145-155mm with the Street at the midpoint. Call at 5pm with a 16% implied move.
AADX reports EPS pre-market on 11/11. Post-market 11/11: AVEX, CAE, CTVA, TTEK. Pre-market 11/12: AIRO, DPC, FPS, LGN, LUNR. Post-market 11/12: HAWK, SPCE, YSS.
